questions.solution:
Pattern followed is:

26 - 50 = (52 + 1) - (72 + 1)

17 - 37 = (42 + 1) - (62 + 1)

65 - 101 = (82 + 1) - (102 + 1)

49 - 82 = (72) - (92 + 1)

questions.question: Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with the commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Some painters are rich.

I. All painters are teachers.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.html: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. All painters are teachers → False (It is possible but not definite)

questions.question: At a party, the number of girls is half the number of boys. After an hour, five boys leave the party and three girls join the party. If the number of boys and girls are equal, then find how many people were present at the party an hour before?
questions.questionHtml: At a party, the number of girls is half the number of boys. After an hour, five boys leave the party and three girls join the party. If the number of boys and girls are equal, then find how many people were present at the party an hour before?
questions.solution:
Let the number of girls at the starting of the party be ‘x’

Then, number of boys = 2 × x = 2x

Given, five boys leave the party and three girls join the party

Number of boys now = 2x – 5

Number of girls = x + 3

According to the question,

(2x – 5) : (x + 3) = 1 : 1

On solving,

x = 8                 

number of girls = 8

number of boys = 8 × 2 = 16

∴ Required number of people = 8 + 16 = 24

Hence, the correct answer is 24.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 24 ÷ 8 – 5 × 5 + 3 = 13
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

24 ÷ 8 – 5 × 5 + 3 = 13
questions.solution:
Interchanging ÷ and ×

24 × 8 - 5 ÷ 5 + 3 = 192 - 1 + 3

194 ≠ 13

Interchanging ÷ and –

\(24 - 8 \div 5 \times 5 + 3 = 24 - \frac{{8 \times 5}}{5} + 3\)

24 - 8 + 3 ≠ 13

Interchanging × and +

24 ÷ 8 - 5 + 5 × 3 = 3 - 5 + 15

-2 + 15 = 13

Interchanging ÷ and +

\(24 + 8 - 5 \times 5 \div 3 = 32 - \frac{{5 \times 5}}{3}\)

\(32 - \frac{{25}}{3} \ne 13\)

Hence by interchanging × and + we get the correct equation.

questions.question: Find the value of2.8 + (0.52 ÷ 0.13 × 2) – 6 × 3 ÷ 8 + 2
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of2.8 + (0.52 ÷ 0.13 × 2) – 6 × 3 ÷ 8 + 2
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order given below ∶

Step-1∶ Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first, and in the bracket,

Step-2∶ Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,

Step-3∶ Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,

Step-4∶ Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be

calculated.      

⇒ 2.8 + (0.52 ÷ 0.13 × 2) – 6 × 3 ÷ 8 + 2

⇒ 2.8 + (4 × 2) – 6 × 3/8 + 2

⇒ 2.8 + 8 – 9/4 + 2

⇒ 12.8 – 2.25

⇒ 10.55

questions.question: In a circle with centre O. AB is the diameter and CD is a chord such that ABCD is a trapezium. If ∠BAC = 25°, then ∠CAD is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O. AB is the diameter and CD is a chord such that ABCD is a trapezium. If ∠BAC = 25°, then ∠CAD is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Given, ∠BAC = 25°

⇒ ∠ACB = 90° [Angle in a semicircle is 90]

In ΔACB

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠CBA + ∠BAC = 180°

⇒ ∠CBA = 180° – 90° – 25° = 65°

⇒ ∠DCA = ∠CAB = 25° [Alternate interior angle]

⇒ ∠DCA = ∠ABD = 25°and ∠CAD = ∠DBC

∵ Two inscribed angles forming the same arc or forming two equal arcs are equal.

⇒ ∠CBA = ∠DBC + ∠ABD

⇒ 65° = ∠DBC + 25°

⇒ ∠DBC = 65° – 25° = 40°

⇒ ∠CAD = ∠DBC = 40°

questions.question: If \(\sqrt x + \frac{1}{{\surd x}} = \sqrt 6 ,\) then \({x^2} + \frac{1}{{{x^2}}}\) is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: If \(\sqrt x + \frac{1}{{\surd x}} = \sqrt 6 ,\) then \({x^2} + \frac{1}{{{x^2}}}\) is equal to∶
questions.solution:
As we know, (x + 1/x)2 = x2 + 1/x2 + 2

Given, √x + 1/√x = √6

⇒ (√x + 1/√x)2 = (√x)2 + (1/√x)2 + 2

⇒ √62 = x + 1/x + 2

⇒ x + 1/x = 6 – 2 = 4

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = x2 + (1/x)2 + 2

⇒ 42 = x2 + 1/x2 + 2

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 16 – 2 = 14

questions.question: A is 40% more efficient than B and C is 20% less efficient than B. Working together, they can finish a task in 15 days. In how many days, will B alone complete 75% of the task?
questions.questionHtml: A is 40% more efficient than B and C is 20% less efficient than B. Working together, they can finish a task in 15 days. In how many days, will B alone complete 75% of the task?
questions.solution:
Let the efficiency of B be 100.

Efficiency of A will be = 100 × [140/100] = 140

Efficiency of C will be = 100 × [80/100] = 80

Efficiency ratio of A, B and C = 140 ∶ 100 ∶ 80 = 7 ∶ 5 ∶ 4

Total work = (7 + 5 + 4) × 15 = 240

75% of total work = 240 × [75/100] = 180

75% of total work B will complete in = 180/5 = 36 days

questions.questionHtml: A train without stoppage travels with an average speed of 65 km/h and with stoppage, it travels with an average speed of 52 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop on an average per hour?
questions.solution:
Without stoppage average speed = 65 km/h

With stoppages average speed = 52 km/h

As we know,

Time of rest per hour equal to the difference in average speed divided by the speed without stoppage.

Required time = [(65 – 52)/65] × 60 = 12

So, A train stops on an average 12 minute/hr

questions.question: If cot θ = 3/4, then sinθ + cosθ – tanθ is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: If cot θ = 3/4, then sinθ + cosθ – tanθ is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Given:

cot θ = 3/4

Concept Used:

Pythagoras theorem, (Hypotenuse)2 = (Base)2 + (Perpendicular)2

⇒ cot θ = Base/perpendicular, sin θ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse, tan θ = Perpendicular/Base

Now, 

⇒ sin θ + cos θ – tan θ

⇒ 4/5 + 3/5 – 4/3 [sin θ = P/H, cos θ = B/H and tanθ = P/B]

questions.question: The price of sugar is increased by 22%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 12% only. By what percent should he decrease his consumption, nearest to one decimal place?
questions.questionHtml: The price of sugar is increased by 22%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 12% only. By what percent should he decrease his consumption, nearest to one decimal place?
questions.solution:
Let the initial price of sugar be 100x.

Price of sugar after increased = 100x × [122/100] = 122x

Person wants his expenditure increase by 12% only, so his expenditure should be = 100x × [112/100] = 112x

Required percentage = [(122 – 112x)/122] × 100 = 8.19% ≈ 8.2%

questions.question: Two articles are sold for Rs. 10,005 each. On one, the seller gains 15% and on the other, he loses 13%. What is his overall gain or loss percent. Correct to two decimal places?
questions.questionHtml: Two articles are sold for Rs. 10,005 each. On one, the seller gains 15% and on the other, he loses 13%. What is his overall gain or loss percent. Correct to two decimal places?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When Selling Price (SP) is same for two articles with gain x% and loss y%:

Overall % = [100(x − y) − 2xy] ÷ [200 + x − y]

Given: x = 15, y = 13

Overall % = [100(15 − 13) − 2(15)(13)] ÷ [200 + 15 − 13] = [200 − 390] ÷ 202 = −190 ÷ 202 ≈ −0.94%

∴ The correct answer is 0.94% loss.

Alternate Method

Given: Selling Price of each article = ₹10,005 | Gain on 1st = 15% | Loss on 2nd = 13%

Formula: Cost Price (CP) = [SP ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss%)] × 100

⇒ CP of Article 1 = 10,005 ÷ 1.15 = ₹8,700

⇒ CP of Article 2 = 10,005 ÷ 0.87 = ₹11,500

⇒ Total CP = 8,700 + 11,500 = ₹20,200

⇒ Total SP = 10,005 + 10,005 = ₹20,010

⇒ Overall Loss = 20,200 − 20,010 = ₹190

⇒ Loss % = (190 ÷ 20,200) × 100 = 190 ÷ 202 ≈ 0.9405%

∴ The correct answer is 0.94% loss.

Additional Information

Standard Equal Profit/Loss Case

If SP is same and there is x% gain and x% loss, there is always a net loss of x2 ÷ 100%.

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (ab/100)]% (not directly applicable here as base CP is different).

Ratio Method

Convert percentage to fractions (15% = 3/20, 13% = 13/100) and equate the SP units to find the combined CP and SP ratio.

questions.question: Chords AB and CD of a circle, when produced, meet at a point P outside the circle, If AB = 6 cm, CD = 3 cm and PD = 5 cm, then PB is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: Chords AB and CD of a circle, when produced, meet at a point P outside the circle, If AB = 6 cm, CD = 3 cm and PD = 5 cm, then PB is equal to∶

⇒ x2 + 6x – 40 = 0

⇒ (x + 10) (x – 4) = 0

⇒ (x + 10) = 0

⇒ x = -10 [not possible]

⇒ (x – 4) = 0

⇒ x = 4

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. There isn't many rice left in the house so we must replenish our stock soon.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

There isn't many rice left in the house so we must replenish our stock soon.
questions.solution:
The word rice is an uncountable noun. Therefore, it is incorrect to quantify it with the adjective many. 

It is instead correct to refer to a quantity of rice with adjectives used for non-countable nouns, such as much or a lot of.

In this sentence, it would be correct to say-- there isn't much rice left.... 

Therefore, the error is in option 4.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The committee reached ______ decision regarding the appointment of the chairman.

Key Points

    • Agreeable - quite enjoyable and pleasurable

  • While all of the other options have positive connotations, none of them fit the context of the sentence in the same way. 
  • Therefore, option 3  is correct.
  • Thus, the complete sentence is: The committee reached a unanimous decision regarding the appointment of the chairman.

questions.question: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The sailors had never encountered such a rough sea.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Such a rough sea had never been encountered by the sailors. 

Key Points  

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice and 'The sailors' is the subject and 'such a rough sea' is the object.
  • When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'The sailors' of the active voice becomes the object, the object 'such a rough sea' becomes the subject.
  • The passive format "had + been + V3 (encountered)" should be used.
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the past perfect tense.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She got a lucrative job of a translator because she was ______ in French
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She got a lucrative job of a translator because she was ______ in French
questions.solution:
The correct answer is proficient

Key Points

Here are the meanings of the given options:

  • Deficient - lacking or not having enough of something. (किसी चीज की कमी)
    • If someone or something is deficient in a particular thing, they do not have the full amount of it that they need in order to function normally or work properly.
    • Example: a diet deficient in vitamin B.
  • Sufficient- enough for a particular purpose. (पर्याप्त)
    • If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.
    • Example: One meter of fabric is sufficient to cover the exterior of an 18-in-diameter hatbox.
  • Proficient -  skilled in doing something. (कुछ करने में कुशल)
    • If you are proficient in something, you can do it well.​
    • Example: A great number of Egyptians are proficient in foreign languages.
  • Efficient - able to perform in a well-planned way. (सुनियोजित तरीके से प्रदर्शन करने में सक्षम)
    • Example: The city's transport system is one of the most efficient in Europe.
  • Out of these, option 3 proficient best fits the context of the sentence.
